# Akadli-AI Full Repository Context for LLMs

This file contains the complete, unedited architectural specifications, agent invariants, and documentation for all packages in the Akadli-AI monorepo (https://akadli.me).


================================================================================
# FILE: AGENTS.md (Architectural Invariants & Agent Guidelines)
================================================================================


# Akadli-AI Agent Guidelines & Architectural Invariants

Canonical architectural reference for stateless AI coding sessions across the Akadli-AI monorepo.

## 1. Project Identity & Namespace
- **Project:** Akadli-AI (Open-source Algerian COD Voice Confirmation Engine & Store Adapters).
- **Scope & Namespaces:** Strictly `@akadli/*` (`@akadli/adapter-contract`, `@akadli/dz-geo`, `@akadli/core`, `@akadli/provider-<name>`, `@akadli/playground`). Never use legacy `@dz-voice/*` or `dz-*` tag prefixes.

## 2. Monorepo Architecture & Package Boundaries
- `packages/adapter-contract`: Pure Zod schemas & TypeScript interfaces (`StandardizedDzOrder`, `FinalizedOrderDecision`, `IEcommerceProvider`). Zero runtime logic.
- `packages/dz-geo`: Official 2026 Algerian administrative divisions (**69 Wilayas, 1,708 Communes**) + `+213` phone normalization.
- `packages/core`: Stateless voice orchestration (`createStandardizedDzOrder`, `buildElevenAgentsDynamicVariables`, `handleFinalizeOrderToolCall`). Note: ElevenLabs system prompts and tool definitions live in the ElevenLabs dashboard, NOT in local code.
- `packages/provider-<name>`: Stateless e-commerce adapters implementing `IEcommerceProvider`. Each provider MUST have:
  - `docs/api-spec.md` & `fixtures/*.json`
  - `src/schemas.ts`, `src/<name>-client.ts`, `src/<name>-provider.ts`, `src/index.ts`
  - `test/<name>-provider.test.ts` (Vitest + MSW `msw/node` covering all 5 mutation/verification scenarios)
- `apps/akadli-playground`: Local HTTPS WebRTC phone & webhook testing sandbox (`/admin` and `/phone`). All store/ERP providers register via `providerRegistry` in `server/src/index.ts`.

## 3. Strict Coding Invariants (Anti-Drift Rules)
- **Zero Bloat Dependencies:** Use Node 20+ native `fetch` and `node:crypto` (`crypto.timingSafeEqual`). Never install `axios`, `node-fetch`, or `moment`.
- **Canonical Order Tags & Notes:**
  - Tags: Always use `akadli-confirmed`, `akadli-modified`, `akadli-refused`, `akadli-variant-{variant}`, and `akadli-qty-{qty}`.
  - Notes: Always prefix automated notes with `[Akadli-AI]`. Zero leftover `dz-confirmed` strings anywhere in `packages/` or `apps/`.
- **No Over-Engineering & Preserve Live Flows:** Keep adapters stateless. Do not break live-verified flows (such as `PhonePage.ts` `onModeChange` goodbye handling or Shopify Algeria `province: null` fallback).

## 4. Mandatory Skills & Verification Gate
- **Skills Reference:** Consult specialized skills in `.agents/skills/`:
  - `dz-monorepo-architect`: Monorepo structure, core voice engine, and contract interfaces.
  - `dz-ecommerce-provider-builder`: Scaffolding and implementing store/ERP providers.
  - `dz-geo-address-normalizer`: Algerian Wilayas/Communes resolution and phone validation.
  - `git-tdd-atomic-workflow`: Pre-commit verification and atomic Conventional Commits.
- **Pre-Commit Verification Gate:** Every task must pass:
  ```bash
  pnpm turbo run build typecheck lint test
  ```
- **Commit Style:** Atomic Conventional Commits (`feat(...)`, `fix(...)`, `docs(...)`, `test(...)`, `chore(...)`).

# FILE: Root README.md

**[English](./README.md) | [🇩🇿 العربية](./README.ar.md)** • [https://akadli.me](https://akadli.me)

# Akadli-AI (`@akadli/*`)

> Open-source Algerian Cash-on-Delivery (COD) Voice Confirmation Engine & E-Commerce Store Adapters.

Akadli-AI automates post-checkout COD order confirmation calls in Algerian Darja via ElevenAgents (WebRTC / SIP / WhatsApp links), validates addresses against the official **2026 Algerian administrative division (69 Wilayas & 1,708 Communes)**, and mutates orders across Shopify, YouCan, WooCommerce, Google Sheets, and Tassyir.

---

## End-to-End Lifecycle

```text
Store Webhook -> @akadli/provider-* (Verify & Parse) -> @akadli/dz-geo (69 Wilayas) -> @akadli/core (Darja Voice Call) -> applyOrderDecision() (Live Store Update)
```

---

## Monorepo Packages

| Package | Scope | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| [`@akadli/adapter-contract`](./packages/adapter-contract) | Contracts | Pure Zod schemas & `IEcommerceProvider` contract |
| [`@akadli/dz-geo`](./packages/dz-geo) | Geo / Phone | 2026 Algerian 69 Wilayas, 1,708 Communes & `+213` phone normalizer |
| [`@akadli/core`](./packages/core) | Core Engine | ElevenAgents dynamic variable builder & `handleFinalizeOrderToolCall` orchestrator |
| [`@akadli/provider-shopify`](./packages/provider-shopify) | Adapter | Shopify HMAC verification, Algeria missing-province fallback, OAuth `client_credentials` & REST mutations |
| [`@akadli/provider-youcan`](./packages/provider-youcan) | Adapter | YouCan `.shop` webhook verification, 1-page COD `extra_fields` parser & order close/update API |
| [`@akadli/provider-woocommerce`](./packages/provider-woocommerce) | Adapter | WooCommerce REST v3 Basic Auth, `DZ-XX` state & COD plugin `meta_data` adapter |
| [`@akadli/provider-gsheets`](./packages/provider-gsheets) | Adapter | Universal Google Sheets v4 & Apps Script bridge for SetShop, JustSell, Foorweb & landing pages |
| [`@akadli/provider-tassyir`](./packages/provider-tassyir) | Adapter / ERP | Tassyir Algerian COD ERP & two-phase courier expedition dispatch for Yalidine/Ecotrack/ZR |

---

## 30-Second Example

```typescript
import { ShopifyProvider } from "@akadli/provider-shopify";
import { handleFinalizeOrderToolCall, buildElevenAgentsDynamicVariables } from "@akadli/core";

const provider = new ShopifyProvider();

// 1. Verify webhook signature & parse standardized Algerian COD order
const isValid = await provider.verifyWebhook(headers, rawBody, process.env.SHOPIFY_WEBHOOK_SECRET!);
const order = await provider.parseWebhookOrder(JSON.parse(rawBody));

// 2. Inject dynamic prompt variables into ElevenAgents for Darja voice confirmation call
const promptVars = buildElevenAgentsDynamicVariables(order);

// 3. Handle ElevenAgents finalize_order_decision tool call & mutate live store
const result = await handleFinalizeOrderToolCall(
  agentToolPayload, // e.g. { orderId: order.orderId, status: "CONFIRMED" }
  provider,
  {
    shopDomain: process.env.SHOPIFY_SHOP_DOMAIN!,
    accessToken: process.env.SHOPIFY_ACCESS_TOKEN!,
  },
  order.constraints
);
```

---

## Interactive Sandbox (`@akadli/playground`)

Test live voice calls over local Wi-Fi with WebRTC audio streaming:

```bash
git clone https://github.com/HarrouAnderrahman/Akadli-AI.git
pnpm install
pnpm build
pnpm --filter @akadli/playground dev
```

- Open `https://localhost:3000/admin` to trigger calls, inspect payloads, and test webhook ingestion.
- Open `https://localhost:3000/phone` on your smartphone to receive simulated customer voice calls.
- See [`packages/provider-shopify/README.md`](./packages/provider-shopify/README.md) for live Shopify Dev Dashboard (`dev.shopify.com`) & Cloudflare Tunnel setup.

---

## For AI Coding Agents

Review [`./AGENTS.md`](./AGENTS.md) and [`.agents/skills/`](./.agents/skills/) before modifying code:
- Maintain `@akadli/*` package boundaries and zero-bloat runtime dependencies.
- Preserve 2026 Wilaya mappings (`01`-`69`) and canonical tags (`akadli-confirmed`, `akadli-modified`, `akadli-refused`).
- Enforce the pre-commit verification gate: `pnpm turbo run build typecheck lint test`.

# Akadli-AI (`@akadli/*`)

> محرك مفتوح المصدر لتأكيد طلبيات الدفع عند الاستلام (COD) صوتياً ومحولات ربط المتاجر الإلكترونية في الجزائر.

يقوم **Akadli-AI** بأتمتة مكالمات تأكيد طلبيات الدفع عند الاستلام (COD) بعد إتمام الطلب بالدارجة الجزائرية عبر ElevenAgents (باستخدام روابط WebRTC / SIP / WhatsApp)، مع التحقق من صحة العناوين وتطبيعها وفق **التقسيم الإداري الجزائري الجديد 2026 (69 ولاية و 1708 بلدية)**، وتحديث بيانات وحالات الطلبات مباشرة عبر المتاجر: Shopify، YouCan، WooCommerce، Google Sheets و Tassyir.

---

## مسار العمل المتكامل (End-to-End Lifecycle)

</div>

<div dir="ltr" align="left">

```text
Store Webhook -> @akadli/provider-* (Verify & Parse) -> @akadli/dz-geo (69 Wilayas) -> @akadli/core (Darja Voice Call) -> applyOrderDecision() (Live Store Update)
```

</div>

<div dir="rtl" align="right">

---

## حزم المستودع (Monorepo Packages)

| الحزمة | النطاق | الوصف |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| [`@akadli/adapter-contract`](./packages/adapter-contract) | العقود البرمجية | مخططات Zod نقية وواجهة `IEcommerceProvider` بدون تبعيات تشغيلية خارجية |
| [`@akadli/dz-geo`](./packages/dz-geo) | الجغرافيا / الهاتف | التقسيم الإداري الجزائري 2026 (69 ولاية و 1708 بلدية) ومعالج أرقام الهاتف `+213` |
| [`@akadli/core`](./packages/core) | المحرك الأساسي | منشئ المتغيرات الديناميكية لـ ElevenAgents ومنسق استدعاءات `handleFinalizeOrderToolCall` |
| [`@akadli/provider-shopify`](./packages/provider-shopify) | محول المتجر | التحقق من توقيع HMAC لـ Shopify، معالجة غياب حقل الولاية، وتبادل OAuth `client_credentials` وتحديثات REST |
| [`@akadli/provider-youcan`](./packages/provider-youcan) | محول المتجر | التحقق من Webhook لـ YouCan `.shop`، واستخراج حقول COD أحادية الصفحة وتحديث وحفظ الطلبات |
| [`@akadli/provider-woocommerce`](./packages/provider-woocommerce) | محول المتجر | واجهة WooCommerce REST v3 وتطبيع رموز الولايات `DZ-XX` وحقول `meta_data` لإضافات COD |
| [`@akadli/provider-gsheets`](./packages/provider-gsheets) | محول الجداول | جسر Google Sheets v4 و Apps Script الشامل لمتاجر SetShop و JustSell و Foorweb وصفحات الهبوط |
| [`@akadli/provider-tassyir`](./packages/provider-tassyir) | محول / ERP | نظام Tassyir الجزائري لإدارة COD وتوزيع الشحنات ثنائي المراحل (Yalidine / Ecotrack / ZR) |

## مثال برمجي في 30 ثانية (TypeScript)

</div>

<div dir="ltr" align="left">

```typescript
import { ShopifyProvider } from "@akadli/provider-shopify";
import { handleFinalizeOrderToolCall, buildElevenAgentsDynamicVariables } from "@akadli/core";

const provider = new ShopifyProvider();

// 1. التحقق من توقيع Webhook وتحليل الطلبية وفق النموذج الجزائري القياسي
const isValid = await provider.verifyWebhook(headers, rawBody, process.env.SHOPIFY_WEBHOOK_SECRET!);
const order = await provider.parseWebhookOrder(JSON.parse(rawBody));

// 2. حقن المتغيرات الديناميكية في ElevenAgents لبدء المكالمة الصوتية بالدارجة
const promptVars = buildElevenAgentsDynamicVariables(order);

// 3. معالجة قرار أداة finalize_order_decision وتحديث المتجر مباشرة
const result = await handleFinalizeOrderToolCall(
  agentToolPayload, // مثلاً: { orderId: order.orderId, status: "CONFIRMED" }
  provider,
  {
    shopDomain: process.env.SHOPIFY_SHOP_DOMAIN!,
    accessToken: process.env.SHOPIFY_ACCESS_TOKEN!,
  },
  order.constraints
);
```

# FILE: @akadli/adapter-contract - README.md
================================================================================


**[English](./README.md) | [🇩🇿 العربية](./README.ar.md)**

# @akadli/adapter-contract

> Zero-dependency canonical Zod schemas and TypeScript interfaces for Algerian COD e-commerce and voice confirmation workflows.

`@akadli/adapter-contract` defines the shared contracts implemented by all store adapters (`@akadli/provider-*`) and consumed by the voice engine (`@akadli/core`).

---

## Exported Schemas & Contracts

| Schema / Interface | Type | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `StandardizedDzOrderSchema` | `StandardizedDzOrder` | Universal order payload normalized across all store providers |
| `FinalizedOrderDecisionSchema` | `FinalizedOrderDecision` | ElevenAgents `finalize_order_decision` payload (`CONFIRMED`, `REFUSED`, `MODIFIED`) |
| `OrderConstraintsSchema` | `OrderConstraints` | Anti-hallucination guardrails (`allowedVariants`, `allowedWilayas`, `allowedCommunes`) |
| `OrderDecisionStatusSchema` | `OrderDecisionStatus` | Enum: `"CONFIRMED" \| "REFUSED" \| "MODIFIED"` |
| `WilayaCodeSchema` | `WilayaCode` | Official zero-padded 2-digit codes (`"01"` to `"69"`) |
| `DzPhoneSchema` | `string` | Regex: `05/06/07XXXXXXXX` (local 10-digit) or `+213[567]XXXXXXXX` (E.164) |
| `IEcommerceProvider` | `interface` | Contract for webhook verification, parsing, and order mutation |
| `ApplyOrderDecisionResult` | `interface` | Standardized result `{ success, externalStatus, rawResponse }` |

---

## Custom Provider Implementation Example

```typescript
import {
  IEcommerceProvider,
  StandardizedDzOrder,
  FinalizedOrderDecision,
  ApplyOrderDecisionResult
} from "@akadli/adapter-contract";

export class CustomStoreProvider implements IEcommerceProvider {
  async verifyWebhook(
    headers: Record<string, string>,
    rawBody: string | Buffer,
    secret: string
  ): Promise<boolean> {
    // Constant-time HMAC or token comparison
    return headers["x-webhook-token"] === secret;
  }

  async parseWebhookOrder(payload: unknown): Promise<StandardizedDzOrder> {
    // Normalize into canonical StandardizedDzOrder using @akadli/dz-geo
    return payload as StandardizedDzOrder;
  }

  async applyOrderDecision(
    orderId: string,
    decision: FinalizedOrderDecision,
    credentials: Record<string, string>
  ): Promise<ApplyOrderDecisionResult> {
    // Mutate store state based on decision.status (CONFIRMED / MODIFIED / REFUSED)
    return { success: true, externalStatus: decision.status };
  }
}
```

---

## Installation

```bash
pnpm add @akadli/adapter-contract
```

# FILE: @akadli/dz-geo - README.md
================================================================================


**[English](./README.md) | [🇩🇿 العربية](./README.ar.md)**

# @akadli/dz-geo

> 2026 Algerian Administrative Divisions (69 Wilayas & 1,708 Communes), fuzzy address resolver, and +213 phone normalizer.

`@akadli/dz-geo` provides official 2026 Algerian geographic data and normalization logic across Arabic, French, and Arabizi inputs for e-commerce checkout forms and voice agent verification.

---

## Core Functions & Exports

| Function / Constant | Returns | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `normalizeWilaya(input)` | `NormalizedWilayaResult` | 4-stage resolver: numbers, canonical script, aliases, Levenshtein fuzzy match |
| `normalizeCommune(raw, code)` | `CommuneMatchResult` | Resolves commune variations against official communes of the Wilaya |
| `normalizeDzPhone(phone, format)` | `string` | Converts Algerian numbers to local (`05/06/07XXXXXXXX`) or E.164 (`+213...`) |
| `getCommunesForWilaya(code)` | `readonly string[]` | List of all official communes for a Wilaya code (`"01"` to `"69"`) |
| `WILAYAS_69` / `WILAYAS_ALL` | `readonly WilayaRecord[]` | Complete 2026 dataset of 69 Wilayas with codes, Arabic/French names, and aliases |
| `WILAYAS_58` | `readonly WilayaRecord[]` | 58-Wilaya backward compatibility slice for legacy couriers |

---

## 2026 Promoted Wilayas (Codes 59–69)

Includes full support for the 11 promoted Wilayas:
- **59**: El Aricha • **60**: Barika • **61**: Ksar Chellala • **62**: Ain Oussera • **63**: Messaad
- **64**: Brizina • **65**: Bir El Ater • **66**: El Kantara • **67**: Ksar El Boukhari • **68**: Bou Saada • **69**: El Abiodh Sidi Cheikh

---

## Usage Example

```typescript
import {
  normalizeWilaya,
  normalizeCommune,
  normalizeDzPhone,
  getCommunesForWilaya
} from "@akadli/dz-geo";

// 1. Phone Normalization
normalizeDzPhone("05 50 12 34 56", "local"); // => "0550123456"
normalizeDzPhone("+213 (0) 661-23-45-67", "e164"); // => "+213661234567"

// 2. Fuzzy Wilaya Matching (Arabic, French, Arabizi, or 5-digit postal code)
normalizeWilaya("بريكة");        // => { code: "60", nameFr: "Barika", nameAr: "بريكة" }
normalizeWilaya("bou saada");    // => { code: "68", nameFr: "Bou Saada", nameAr: "بوسعادة" }
normalizeWilaya("13000");        // => { code: "13", nameFr: "Tlemcen", nameAr: "تلمسان" }

// 3. Commune Resolution within Wilaya
const result = normalizeCommune("maghnia", "13");
console.log(result.canonicalCommune); // => "Maghnia"
```

---

## Installation

```bash
pnpm add @akadli/dz-geo
```

# FILE: @akadli/core - README.md
================================================================================


**[English](./README.md) | [🇩🇿 العربية](./README.ar.md)**

# @akadli/core

> Stateless orchestration engine connecting ElevenLabs Conversational AI (ElevenAgents) with Algerian COD store providers.

`@akadli/core` bridges incoming e-commerce orders, voice prompt variable injection, and post-call order finalization decisions without maintaining persistent server-side call state.

---

## Core Functions & Exports

| Function | Signature | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `createStandardizedDzOrder(params)` | `StandardizedDzOrder` | Normalizes phone, Wilaya, and commune via `@akadli/dz-geo` and sets validation constraints |
| `buildElevenAgentsDynamicVariables(order)` | `ElevenAgentsDynamicVariables` | Generates prompt variables (`customer_phone_e164`, `price_da`, `allowed_variants`, `allowed_wilayas`, `allowed_communes`) |
| `handleFinalizeOrderToolCall(payload, provider, creds, constraints)` | `Promise<FinalizeOrderToolResult>` | Validates `finalize_order_decision` tool calls, checks constraints, and calls `provider.applyOrderDecision` |

---

## ElevenAgents Integration Flow

```text
StandardizedDzOrder -> buildElevenAgentsDynamicVariables() -> ElevenLabs WebRTC Call -> finalize_order_decision Tool -> handleFinalizeOrderToolCall() -> Provider Mutation
```

---

## Usage Example

```typescript
import {
  createStandardizedDzOrder,
  buildElevenAgentsDynamicVariables,
  handleFinalizeOrderToolCall
} from "@akadli/core";
import { ShopifyProvider } from "@akadli/provider-shopify";

// 1. Create a standardized Algerian COD order
const order = createStandardizedDzOrder({
  orderId: "1001",
  storeName: "Algeria Store",
  customerName: "Karim Ziani",
  rawCustomerPhone: "0550123456",
  itemName: "Sneakers Air Max",
  priceDa: 4500,
  currentVariant: "42",
  rawWilaya: "Barika",
  rawCommune: "Barika",
  allowedVariants: ["41", "42", "43"]
});

// 2. Build dynamic variables for ElevenAgents prompt
const promptVariables = buildElevenAgentsDynamicVariables(order);

// 3. Handle finalize_order_decision tool call from the agent
const provider = new ShopifyProvider();
const result = await handleFinalizeOrderToolCall(
  {
    orderId: "1001",
    status: "CONFIRMED",
    reasonOrNotes: "Confirmed by Karim over phone"
  },
  provider,
  {
    shopDomain: "store.myshopify.com",
    accessToken: "shpat_xxxxxxxx"
  },
  order.constraints
);

console.log(result.success, result.externalStatus);
```

---

## Installation

```bash
pnpm add @akadli/core
```

# FILE: @akadli/provider-shopify - README.md
================================================================================


**[English](./README.md) | [🇩🇿 العربية](./README.ar.md)**

# @akadli/provider-shopify

> Shopify Cash-On-Delivery (COD) adapter with 2026 Algerian address resolution, HMAC-SHA256 verification, and REST order mutations.

Implements `IEcommerceProvider` from `@akadli/adapter-contract` for Shopify stores using standard checkout or Algerian 1-page checkout apps (EasySell, Releasit, CodForm).

---

## 2026 Shopify Dev Dashboard Setup Guide

1. **Create App:** Navigate to [dev.shopify.com](https://dev.shopify.com) -> **Apps** -> **Create an App**.
   - App URL: `https://example.com` (leave **Embed app in Shopify admin** **UNCHECKED**).
   - Scopes: In **API access**, grant `read_orders` and `write_orders`.
2. **Enable Protected Customer Data Access (CRITICAL):**
   - In **API access** -> **Protected customer data access**, enable **Name**, **Address**, and **Phone**.
   - *Without this, Shopify redacts customer details from webhooks and blocks shipping address updates.*
3. **Configure Webhook:**
   - In Shopify Admin -> **Settings** -> **Notifications** -> **Webhooks**, create an `Order creation` JSON webhook pointing to `/api/webhooks/shopify`.
4. **Algerian Address Fallback (`province: null`):**
   - Standard Shopify checkout hides the state/province dropdown for Algeria. Customers input Wilayas in `city`, `address1`, or 5-digit `zip` (`13000` -> Wilaya `13`). COD apps store details in `note_attributes`. `@akadli/provider-shopify` extracts and normalizes all candidates via `@akadli/dz-geo`.

---

## Credentials Schema (`ShopifyCredentialsSchema`)

| Field | Type | Required | Default | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `shopDomain` | `string` | Yes | — | Shopify domain (e.g., `store.myshopify.com`) |
| `accessToken` | `string` | Optional* | — | Permanent Admin API token (`shpat_...`) |
| `clientId` | `string` | Optional* | — | OAuth Client ID (auto-exchanged for token) |
| `clientSecret` | `string` | Optional* | — | OAuth Client Secret |
| `apiVersion` | `string` | No | `"2024-04"` | Shopify Admin REST API version |
| `cancelOnRefused` | `string` | No | `"true"` | Cancels order on `REFUSED` decision |

*\*Must provide either `accessToken` OR both `clientId` and `clientSecret`.*

---

## Usage Example

```typescript
import { ShopifyProvider } from "@akadli/provider-shopify";

const provider = new ShopifyProvider();

// 1. Verify Webhook HMAC signature (Base64)
const isValid = await provider.verifyWebhook(headers, rawBody, process.env.SHOPIFY_WEBHOOK_SECRET!);

// 2. Parse standardized Algerian COD order
const order = await provider.parseWebhookOrder(JSON.parse(rawBody));

// 3. Apply post-call decision to Shopify (tags: akadli-confirmed / akadli-modified / akadli-refused)
const result = await provider.applyOrderDecision(order.orderId, {
  orderId: order.orderId,
  status: "CONFIRMED",
  reasonOrNotes: "Confirmed via voice agent"
}, {
  shopDomain: process.env.SHOPIFY_SHOP_DOMAIN!,
  accessToken: process.env.SHOPIFY_ACCESS_TOKEN!
});
```

# FILE: @akadli/provider-shopify - docs/api-spec.md

# Shopify COD Order Confirmation Adapter Specification (`@akadli/provider-shopify`)

This document defines the technical specification, webhook signature verification, Algerian COD data extraction, and outbound mutation endpoints for Shopify stores integrating with the **Akadli-AI** voice confirmation engine.

---

## Live Shopify Store Setup Guide (2026 Dev Dashboard)

This section covers the verified live setup steps for integrating Shopify stores with Akadli-AI:

### 1. Create App in `dev.shopify.com`
- Navigate to [dev.shopify.com](https://dev.shopify.com) and create or open your app.
- Set **App URL** to `https://example.com` (leave **Embed app in Shopify admin** **UNCHECKED**).
- Under **API access** -> **Scopes**, select `read_orders,write_orders`.

### 2. Enable Protected Customer Data Access (CRITICAL)
- In `dev.shopify.com` -> **API access** -> **Protected customer data access**, enable **Protected customer data**.
- Check **Name**, **Address**, and **Phone**.
- *Rationale*: Shopify redacts customer details from webhooks and blocks `shipping_address` mutations if these fields are not explicitly approved.

### 3. Authentication (`clientId` + `clientSecret` or `accessToken`)
- **OAuth Exchange**: Provide `SHOPIFY_CLIENT_ID` and `SHOPIFY_CLIENT_SECRET`. `@akadli/provider-shopify` automatically requests an access token from `POST /admin/oauth/access_token` with `grant_type: client_credentials` and caches it in memory until expiry.
- **Direct Access Token**: Alternatively, configure `SHOPIFY_ACCESS_TOKEN` (`shpat_...`) directly.

### 4. Algerian Address Mapping (Missing `Province` Field)
- Shopify checkout hides the `Province` field when Country is set to `Algeria`.
- Customers typically provide their Wilaya in `city`, `address1`, or enter a 5-digit Algerian ONP postal code in `zip` (`13000` -> Wilaya `13`).
- Many Algerian merchants use COD form apps (EasySell, Releasit) which store address fields in `note_attributes`.
- `@akadli/provider-shopify` dynamically resolves Wilaya and Commune using multi-candidate resolution across `note_attributes`, `province`/`province_code`, `city`, `zip`, and `address1`/`address2` via `@akadli/dz-geo`.

---

## 1. Webhook Signature Verification (`verifyWebhook`)

Shopify signs every webhook request using HMAC-SHA256 calculated over the unparsed raw request body with the merchant's webhook shared secret.

### Specifications
- **Header:** `X-Shopify-Hmac-Sha256` (case-insensitive extraction via `headers["x-shopify-hmac-sha256"]`).
- **Algorithm:** `sha256` HMAC encoded as **Base64**.
- **Timing Attack Prevention:** Comparison must be performed using `crypto.timingSafeEqual` over buffers of equal byte length.
- **Fail Safe:** If the header is missing, lengths mismatch, or the digest does not match, return `false` without throwing uncaught exceptions.

```typescript
import { createHmac, timingSafeEqual } from "node:crypto";

export function verifyShopifyWebhook(
  headers: Record<string, string>,
  rawBody: string | Buffer,
  secret: string
): boolean {
  const headerKey = Object.keys(headers).find(
    (k) => k.toLowerCase() === "x-shopify-hmac-sha256"
  );
  const signature = headerKey ? headers[headerKey] : undefined;
  if (!signature || !secret) return false;

  const bodyBuffer = typeof rawBody === "string" ? Buffer.from(rawBody, "utf8") : rawBody;
  const hmac = createHmac("sha256", secret).update(bodyBuffer).digest("base64");

  const sigBuffer = Buffer.from(signature, "utf8");
  const hmacBuffer = Buffer.from(hmac, "utf8");

  if (sigBuffer.length !== hmacBuffer.length) return false;
  return timingSafeEqual(sigBuffer, hmacBuffer);
}
```

---

## 2. Inbound COD Order Extraction (`parseWebhookOrder`)

Shopify `orders/create` payloads for Algerian cash-on-delivery merchants arrive in two primary forms:
1. **Standard Shopify Checkout:** Customer address and phone are located in `shipping_address` or `billing_address`.
2. **Algerian COD Form Apps (EasySell, Releasit, CodForm, FastForm):** Because checkout is bypassed, `shipping_address` is frequently blank, partial, or generic. The true customer phone, Wilaya, and Commune are stored in `note_attributes` key-value pairs.

### Extraction Pipeline
1. **Order ID & Basics:**
   - `orderId`: `String(payload.id)`
   - `storeName`: `payload.shop_name || payload.store_name || "Shopify Store"`
   - `itemName`: First line item title (`payload.line_items?.[0]?.title || "Article"`)
   - `currentVariant`: First line item variant title (`payload.line_items?.[0]?.variant_title || "Standard"`)
   - `priceDa`: `Math.round(Number(payload.total_price || 0))`

2. **Dual-Source Address & Phone Fallback:**
   Scan `shipping_address`, `billing_address`, and `note_attributes` (case-insensitive substring match):
   - **Phone:** `shipping_address.phone` $\rightarrow$ `billing_address.phone` $\rightarrow$ `customer.phone` $\rightarrow$ `note_attributes` matching `phone`, `téléphone`, `telephone`, `tel`, or `هاتف`.
   - **Wilaya:** `shipping_address.province` $\rightarrow$ `shipping_address.province_code` $\rightarrow$ `note_attributes` matching `wilaya`, `province`, or `ولاية`.
   - **Commune:** `shipping_address.city` $\rightarrow$ `note_attributes` matching `commune`, `city`, or `بلدية`.
   - **Customer Name:** `shipping_address.name` $\rightarrow$ `${customer.first_name} ${customer.last_name}` $\rightarrow$ `note_attributes` matching `nom`, `name`, or `اسم` $\rightarrow$ `"Client"`.
   - **Address Note:** `shipping_address.address1` $\rightarrow$ `note_attributes` matching `adresse`, `address`, or `عنوان`.

3. **Normalization via `@akadli/dz-geo` & `@akadli/core`:**
   - Phone is normalized to 10-digit local format (`05/06/07XXXXXXXX`) via `normalizeDzPhone(..., "local")`.
   - Wilaya is matched against all 69 official 2026 Wilayas via `normalizeWilaya(...)`.
   - Commune is resolved and verified for that Wilaya via `normalizeCommune(..., wilayaCode)`.
   - Constraints (`allowedWilayas`, `allowedCommunes`, `allowedVariants`) are populated and validated using `createStandardizedDzOrder(...)`.

---

## 3. Order Decision Mutation (`applyOrderDecision`)

Once the customer completes the ElevenAgents voice confirmation call, the decision is mutated in Shopify Admin API.

### Required Credentials
```typescript
export interface ShopifyProviderCredentials {
  shopDomain: string;       // e.g. "store.myshopify.com"
  accessToken: string;      // Shopify Admin Access Token ("shpat_...")
  apiVersion?: string;      // defaults to "2024-04"
  cancelOnRefused?: string; // "true" (default) or "false"
}
```

### Mutation Endpoints

#### 1. `CONFIRMED`
- **Method:** `PUT https://{shopDomain}/admin/api/{apiVersion}/orders/{orderId}.json`
- **Headers:** `X-Shopify-Access-Token: {accessToken}`, `Content-Type: application/json`
- **Payload:**
```json
{
  "order": {
    "id": 1029384756,
    "tags": "akadli-confirmed",
    "note": "[Akadli-AI] Order CONFIRMED by customer."
  }
}
```

#### 2. `MODIFIED`
- **Method:** `PUT https://{shopDomain}/admin/api/{apiVersion}/orders/{orderId}.json`
- **Headers:** `X-Shopify-Access-Token: {accessToken}`, `Content-Type: application/json`
- **Payload:**
```json
{
  "order": {
    "id": 1029384756,
    "tags": "akadli-modified, akadli-variant-43",
    "note": "[Akadli-AI] Order MODIFIED: Variant -> 43; Commune -> Maghnia; Note -> Près de la mosquée.",
    "shipping_address": {
      "province": "13",
      "city": "Maghnia",
      "address1": "Près de la mosquée"
    }
  }
}
```

#### 3. `REFUSED`
- **Step A:** `PUT https://{shopDomain}/admin/api/{apiVersion}/orders/{orderId}.json` with tag `"akadli-refused"` and refusal note.
- **Step B (if `cancelOnRefused !== "false"`):** `POST https://{shopDomain}/admin/api/{apiVersion}/orders/{orderId}/cancel.json`
- **Headers:** `X-Shopify-Access-Token: {accessToken}`, `Content-Type: application/json`
- **Cancel Payload:**
```json
{
  "reason": "customer",
  "email": false,
  "restock": true
}
```

---

## 4. Error Handling & Resilience
- **401 Unauthorized:** Return `{ success: false, externalStatus: "UNAUTHORIZED", rawResponse: ... }`.
- **404 Not Found:** Return `{ success: false, externalStatus: "NOT_FOUND", rawResponse: ... }`.
- **429 Too Many Requests:** Check `Retry-After` header and handle rate limiting gracefully.
- **5xx Server Errors:** Return descriptive error message with HTTP status code.

# @akadli/provider-youcan

> YouCan (.shop) Cash-On-Delivery (COD) adapter with Algerian 1-page checkout parsing, HMAC-SHA256 signature verification, and REST order mutations.

Implements `IEcommerceProvider` from `@akadli/adapter-contract` for YouCan stores operating in Algeria.

---

## YouCan Seller Area Setup Guide

1. **Generate API Token:** In [seller-area.youcan.shop](https://seller-area.youcan.shop), go to **Settings** -> **API & Integrations** and generate an API Access Token.
2. **Configure Webhook:**
   - In **Settings** -> **Webhooks**, create a new webhook for the event `order.created`.
   - Set the URL to your endpoint (e.g. `https://your-domain.com/api/webhooks/youcan`).
   - Copy the generated Webhook Secret (`x-youcan-signature` hex digest verification).
3. **Algerian 1-Page COD Parsing:**
   - In Algeria, YouCan merchants often use single-page checkout forms where customer inputs are stored inside `extra_fields` or `custom_fields`.
   - `@akadli/provider-youcan` automatically extracts address information from both standard `shipping.address` and `extra_fields` / `custom_fields`, normalizing the Wilaya (`01`-`69`) and commune via `@akadli/dz-geo`.

---

| Field | Type | Required | Default | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `accessToken` | `string` | Yes | — | YouCan API Access Token |
| `baseUrl` | `string` | No | `"https://api.youcan.shop"` | YouCan REST API base URL |
| `closeOnRefused` | `string` | No | `"true"` | Closes/cancels the order if customer refuses call |

---

## Usage Example

```typescript
import { YouCanProvider } from "@akadli/provider-youcan";

const provider = new YouCanProvider();

// 1. Verify Webhook HMAC signature (hex digest from x-youcan-signature)
const isValid = await provider.verifyWebhook(headers, rawBody, process.env.YOUCAN_WEBHOOK_SECRET!);

// 2. Parse standardized Algerian COD order (supports shipping.address & extra_fields)
const order = await provider.parseWebhookOrder(JSON.parse(rawBody));

// 3. Mutate YouCan order after confirmation call (tags: akadli-confirmed / akadli-modified / akadli-refused)
const result = await provider.applyOrderDecision(order.orderId, {
  orderId: order.orderId,
  status: "CONFIRMED",
  reasonOrNotes: "Confirmed via voice call"
}, {
  accessToken: process.env.YOUCAN_ACCESS_TOKEN!
});
```

# FILE: @akadli/provider-youcan - docs/api-spec.md

# YouCan COD Order Confirmation Adapter Specification (`@akadli/provider-youcan`)

This document defines the technical specification, webhook signature verification, Algerian COD data extraction, and outbound mutation endpoints for YouCan (`.shop`) stores integrating with the **Akadli-AI** voice confirmation engine.

---

## 1. Webhook Signature Verification (`verifyWebhook`)

YouCan signs webhook payloads using HMAC-SHA256 computed over the untouched raw request body with the merchant's webhook secret key.

### Specifications
- **Header:** `x-youcan-signature` (case-insensitive extraction via case-insensitive header lookup).
- **Algorithm:** `sha256` HMAC encoded as a lowercase **hex** string.
- **Timing Attack Prevention:** Comparison must be performed using `crypto.timingSafeEqual` between buffers of equal byte length.
- **Fail Safe:** If the header is missing, lengths mismatch, or signature is invalid, return `false` without throwing unhandled exceptions.

```typescript
import { createHmac, timingSafeEqual } from "node:crypto";

export function verifyYouCanWebhook(
  headers: Record<string, string>,
  rawBody: string | Buffer,
  secret: string
): boolean {
  const headerKey = Object.keys(headers).find(
    (k) => k.toLowerCase() === "x-youcan-signature"
  );
  const signature = headerKey ? headers[headerKey] : undefined;
  if (!signature || !secret) return false;

  const bodyBuffer = typeof rawBody === "string" ? Buffer.from(rawBody, "utf8") : rawBody;
  const hmacHex = createHmac("sha256", secret).update(bodyBuffer).digest("hex");

  const sigBuffer = Buffer.from(signature, "utf8");
  const hmacBuffer = Buffer.from(hmacHex, "utf8");

  if (sigBuffer.length !== hmacBuffer.length) return false;
  return timingSafeEqual(sigBuffer, hmacBuffer);
}
```

---

## 2. Inbound COD Order Extraction (`parseWebhookOrder`)

YouCan webhook deliveries can arrive in several envelope formats:

1. **Official YouCan Resthook Standard Payload Format:**
   ```json
   {
     "event_name": "order.created",
     "event_happened_at": "2026-10-16T14:20:00.000000Z",
     "data": {
       "id": "ord_yc_882910",
       "total": 6400,
       ...
     }
   }
   ```
2. **App Webhook / Resthook Delivery Envelope:**
   ```json
   {
     "id": "8e6b019b-06de-496d-a96d-c9ee69c0ccf0",
     "event": "order.created",
     "store_id": "store_yc_111",
     "payload": {
       "id": "ord_yc_882910",
       ...
     }
   }
   ```
3. **Nested Resource Envelope:** `{ data: { order: { ... } } }`, `{ payload: { order: { ... } } }`, or `{ order: { ... } }`.
4. **Direct Order Object:** `{ id: "ord_yc_882910", total: ..., customer: { ... }, shipping: { ... } }`.

### Extraction Pipeline

1. **Envelope Unwrapping & ID Resolution (`unwrapYouCanPayload`):**
   - Automatically unwrap `data.order`, `data`, `payload.order`, `payload`, or `order`.
   - In Resthook delivery envelopes, the root `id` is the webhook delivery UUID. The actual order identifier is resolved from `orderData.id`, `orderData.order_id`, or `orderData.ref`.
   - Preserves top-level metadata (`store_name`, `extra_fields`, `custom_fields`, `customer`, `notes`).
   - Normalizes flattened `shipping` objects into canonical `{ address: { ... } }`.

2. **Order Basics & Line Item Extraction:**
   - `orderId`: `String(data.id)`
   - `storeName`: `data.store_name || data.shop_name || "YouCan Store"`
   - `priceDa`: `Math.round(Number(data.total || 0))`
   - **Product Name (`itemName`) Resolution (in priority order):**
     1. `variants[0]?.variant?.product?.name`
     2. `variants[0]?.variant?.product?.meta?.title`
     3. `variants[0]?.item?.name`
     4. `variants[0]?.name` / `variants[0]?.title`
     5. `line_items[0]?.title` / `line_items[0]?.name`
     6. Fallback: `"Article"`
   - **Selected Variant (`currentVariant`) Resolution (in priority order):**
     1. Case-insensitive lookup in `variants[0]?.variant?.variations` (for keys matching `variant`, `size`, `taille`, `pointure`, `مقاس`, or first non-default string value)
     2. `variants[0]?.variant?.values?.[0]` (if not `"default"`)
     3. `variants[0]?.variation` (case-insensitive key lookup)
     4. `variants[0]?.title` / `variants[0]?.variant?.title` / `line_items[0]?.variant_title`
     5. Fallback: `"Standard"`
   - **Allowed Variants (`allowedVariants`) Extraction:**
     - Inspect `variants[0]?.variant?.product?.variant_options`
     - Extract values from the option matching `/^(?:size|taille|pointure|مقاس|variant)$/i` (or first option with non-empty string values array, e.g. `["M", "L", "XL"]`)
     - Ensure `currentVariant` is always included in `allowedVariants`
     - Populates `constraints.allowedVariants` in `createStandardizedDzOrder`

3. **Resilient Multi-Candidate Algerian Address & Phone Extraction:**
   - **Phone Extraction:**
     - Primary: `shipping.address.phone` or `shipping.phone` or `customer.phone`
     - Fallback: `extra_fields` / `custom_fields` or customer notes matching `/(?:phone|téléphone|telephone|tel|mobile|هاتف|تلفون|موبايل|جوال)/i`
   - **Multi-Candidate Wilaya Resolution:**
     - Try in order: `extra_fields`/`custom_fields` -> `customer_notes` -> `shipping.address.region` -> `shipping.address.state` -> `shipping.address.city` -> `zip` (5-digit prefix or 2-digit code) -> `first_line`/`address1` -> `second_line`/`address2`.
     - Validates against all 69 official 2026 Wilayas via `normalizeWilaya(...)`.
   - **Smart Commune Resolution:**
     - Once Wilaya is resolved, checks `extra_fields`, `customer_notes`, `city`, `first_line`, and `second_line` against `normalizeCommune(..., wilayaCode)`.
     - Prioritizes specific non-capital communes over the Wilaya capital when found in street lines.

4. **Normalization via `@akadli/dz-geo` & `@akadli/core`:**
   - Phone is normalized to 10-digit local format (`05/06/07XXXXXXXX`) via `normalizeDzPhone(..., "local")`.
   - Populates `constraints` (`allowedWilayas`, `allowedCommunes`, `allowedVariants`) and builds a canonical `StandardizedDzOrder`.

---

## 3. Order Decision Mutation (`applyOrderDecision`)

Once the customer concludes the voice confirmation call, the decision is updated in the YouCan REST API.

### Required Credentials
```typescript
export interface YouCanCredentials {
  accessToken: string;       // YouCan API Access Token (Bearer auth)
  baseUrl?: string;          // Default: "https://api.youcan.shop"
  closeOnRefused?: string;   // Default: "true" ("false" to skip /orders/{id}/close)
}
```

### Outbound REST Endpoints

All requests include headers:
- `Authorization: Bearer {accessToken}`
- `Content-Type: application/json`
- `Accept: application/json`

#### 1. `CONFIRMED`
- **Method:** `PUT {baseUrl}/orders/{orderId}`
- **Payload:**
```json
{
  "tags": ["akadli-confirmed"],
  "notes": "[Akadli-AI] Order CONFIRMED by customer."
}
```
- **Returns:** `{ success: true, externalStatus: "CONFIRMED", rawResponse: ... }`

#### 2. `MODIFIED`
- **Method:** `PUT {baseUrl}/orders/{orderId}`
- **Payload:**
```json
{
  "shipping": {
    "address": {
      "region": "13",
      "city": "Mansourah",
      "first_line": "Near Pharmacie Centrale"
    }
  },
  "tags": ["akadli-modified", "akadli-variant-XL"],
  "notes": "[Akadli-AI] Order MODIFIED: Variant -> XL; Wilaya -> 13; Commune -> Mansourah; Note -> Near Pharmacie Centrale; Details: Customer requested XL"
}
```
- **Returns:** `{ success: true, externalStatus: "UPDATED_AND_CONFIRMED", rawResponse: ... }`

#### 3. `REFUSED`
- **Step A:** `PUT {baseUrl}/orders/{orderId}`
```json
{
  "tags": ["akadli-refused"],
  "notes": "[Akadli-AI] Order REFUSED: Customer cancelled on call."
}
```
- **Step B:** If `credentials.closeOnRefused !== "false"`, call:
  - **Method:** `PUT {baseUrl}/orders/{orderId}/close`
  - **Payload:** `{"cancel_order": true}`
  - Closes the refused order and returns items back to stock.
- **Returns:** `{ success: true, externalStatus: "CANCELLED", rawResponse: ... }`

#### 4. Additional Status Updates (`YouCanClient.updateOrderStatus`)
- **Method:** `PUT {baseUrl}/orders/{orderId}/status`
- **Payload:** `{"status": "processed"}` (or `"open"`, `"closed"`, `"canceled-by-seller"`)

---

## 4. HTTP Error Handling

- **401 Unauthorized / 403 Forbidden**: Invalid or expired `accessToken`. Fails immediately without retries.
- **404 Not Found**: Order does not exist on YouCan.
- **422 Unprocessable Entity**: Invalid order field or state transition.
- **429 Too Many Requests / 5xx Server Error**: Retried up to 3 times with exponential backoff before failing.

**[English](./README.md) | [🇩🇿 العربية](./README.ar.md)**

# @akadli/provider-woocommerce

> WooCommerce Cash-On-Delivery (COD) adapter with DZ-XX state code mapping, COD plugin meta_data extraction, HMAC-SHA256 verification, and REST v3 order mutations.

Implements `IEcommerceProvider` from `@akadli/adapter-contract` for WordPress WooCommerce stores operating in Algeria.

---

## WooCommerce & WordPress Setup Guide

1. **Generate REST API Keys:**
   - In WP Admin, navigate to **WooCommerce** -> **Settings** -> **Advanced** -> **REST API**.
   - Click **Add Key**: Set description to `Akadli-AI`, select user, and set Permissions to **Read/Write**.
   - Copy the generated `Consumer key` (`ck_...`) and `Consumer secret` (`cs_...`).
2. **Configure Webhook:**
   - In WP Admin -> **WooCommerce** -> **Settings** -> **Advanced** -> **Webhooks**, click **Add Webhook**.
   - Status: **Active** • Topic: **Order created** • Delivery URL: `https://your-domain.com/api/webhooks/woocommerce`.
   - Secret: Enter your signing secret (used for Base64 `x-wc-webhook-signature` verification).
   - API Version: **WP REST API Integration v3**.
3. **Algerian `DZ-XX` States & COD Plugins:**
   - Standard WooCommerce represents Algerian Wilayas as `DZ-XX` state codes (e.g. `DZ-16` for Alger, `DZ-68` for Bou Saada).
   - Stores using Algerian COD checkout plugins store custom entries in order `meta_data` (e.g., `_billing_wilaya`, `_shipping_commune`).
   - `@akadli/provider-woocommerce` parses both standard address objects and plugin `meta_data` into canonical `@akadli/dz-geo` Wilayas (`01`-`69`).

---

## Credentials Schema (`WooCommerceCredentialsSchema`)

| Field | Type | Required | Default | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `siteUrl` | `string` | Yes | — | WordPress site URL (e.g., `https://dz-store.com`) |
| `consumerKey` | `string` | Yes | — | WooCommerce REST API Consumer Key (`ck_...`) |
| `consumerSecret` | `string` | Yes | — | WooCommerce REST API Consumer Secret (`cs_...`) |
| `cancelOnRefused` | `string` | No | `"true"` | Sets order status to `cancelled` upon `REFUSED` decision |

---

## Usage Example

```typescript
import { WooCommerceProvider, isWooCommerceWebhookPing } from "@akadli/provider-woocommerce";

const provider = new WooCommerceProvider();

// 1. Acknowledge WooCommerce initial unsigned handshake ping (WC_Webhook::deliver_ping)
if (isWooCommerceWebhookPing(headers, req.body, rawBody)) {
  return res.status(200).json({ success: true, message: "Webhook ping acknowledged" });
}

// 2. Verify Webhook HMAC signature (Base64 from x-wc-webhook-signature)
const isValid = await provider.verifyWebhook(headers, rawBody, process.env.WOOCOMMERCE_WEBHOOK_SECRET!);
if (!isValid) {
  return res.status(401).json({ error: "Invalid HMAC signature" });
}

// 3. Parse standardized Algerian COD order (supports DZ-XX states and meta_data)
const order = await provider.parseWebhookOrder(JSON.parse(rawBody));

// 4. Mutate WooCommerce order (updates meta_data, adds order note, updates status)
const result = await provider.applyOrderDecision(order.orderId, {
  orderId: order.orderId,
  status: "CONFIRMED",
  reasonOrNotes: "Customer confirmed via phone"
}, {
  siteUrl: process.env.WOOCOMMERCE_SITE_URL!,
  consumerKey: process.env.WOOCOMMERCE_CONSUMER_KEY!,
  consumerSecret: process.env.WOOCOMMERCE_CONSUMER_SECRET!
});
```

# FILE: @akadli/provider-woocommerce - docs/api-spec.md

# WooCommerce COD Order Confirmation Adapter Specification (`@akadli/provider-woocommerce`)

This document defines the technical specification, webhook signature verification, Algerian COD data extraction, and outbound mutation endpoints for WooCommerce stores integrating with the **Akadli-AI** voice confirmation engine.

---

## 1. Webhook Signature Verification (`verifyWebhook`)

WooCommerce signs webhook payloads using HMAC-SHA256 computed over the untouched raw request body with the merchant's configured webhook secret key.

### Specifications
- **Header:** `x-wc-webhook-signature` (case-insensitive extraction via case-insensitive header lookup).
- **Algorithm:** `sha256` HMAC encoded as a **Base64** string.
- **Timing Attack Prevention:** Comparison must be performed using `crypto.timingSafeEqual` between buffers of equal byte length.
- **Fail Safe:** If the header is missing, lengths mismatch, or signature is invalid, return `false` without throwing unhandled exceptions.

```typescript
import { createHmac, timingSafeEqual } from "node:crypto";

export function verifyWooCommerceWebhook(
  headers: Record<string, string>,
  rawBody: string | Buffer,
  secret: string
): boolean {
  const headerKey = Object.keys(headers).find(
    (k) => k.toLowerCase() === "x-wc-webhook-signature"
  );
  const signature = headerKey ? headers[headerKey] : undefined;
  if (!signature || !secret) return false;

  const bodyBuffer = typeof rawBody === "string" ? Buffer.from(rawBody, "utf8") : rawBody;
  const hmacBase64 = createHmac("sha256", secret).update(bodyBuffer).digest("base64");

  const sigBuffer = Buffer.from(signature, "utf8");
  const hmacBuffer = Buffer.from(hmacBase64, "utf8");

  if (sigBuffer.length !== hmacBuffer.length) return false;
  return timingSafeEqual(sigBuffer, hmacBuffer);
}
```

### Initial Unsigned Handshake Ping (`isWooCommerceWebhookPing`)
When creating or activating a webhook in WordPress Admin, WooCommerce core invokes `WC_Webhook::deliver_ping()` via `wp_safe_remote_post()`.
- **Payload:** `webhook_id=<id>` (sent with `Content-Type: application/x-www-form-urlencoded`).
- **Signature:** WooCommerce **does not calculate or send** an `x-wc-webhook-signature` header on test pings.
- **Handling:** Webhook receivers must recognize this handshake via `isWooCommerceWebhookPing(headers, body, rawBody)` and acknowledge immediately with HTTP 200 without attempting HMAC verification or order parsing.

---

## 2. Inbound COD Order Extraction (`parseWebhookOrder`)

WooCommerce `order.created` or `order.updated` payloads for Algerian COD merchants typically arrive in one of two modes:
1. **Standard WooCommerce Checkout:** Customer address and phone are located in `billing` and `shipping` objects (`state` formatted as `"DZ-13"`, `"13"`, or `"Tlemcen"`, `city` for Commune, `address_1`/`address_2` for street notes, `phone`, and `postcode`).
2. **Algerian COD Checkout Plugins (WooCommerce Dz, Yalidine WooCommerce, EasyCOD, etc.):** Because merchants in Algeria frequently replace the standard multi-step checkout with a simplified single-form COD plugin, customer phone, Wilaya, and Commune are frequently stored in top-level `meta_data` (e.g. `_billing_wilaya`, `wilaya`, `commune`, `baladiya`, `_billing_phone`).

### Extraction Pipeline

1. **Order Basics:**
   - `orderId`: `String(payload.id)`
   - `storeName`: `payload.store_name || "WooCommerce Store"`
   - `itemName`: First line item title (`payload.line_items?.[0]?.name || "Article"`)
   - `currentVariant`: Extracted by scanning `line_items[0]?.meta_data` for keys matching `/(?:pa_size|size|taille|pointure|variant|pa_variant)/i` or variant name/title, defaulting to `"Standard"`.
   - `priceDa`: `Math.round(Number(payload.total || 0))`

2. **Multi-Source Address & Phone Extraction (Standard + COD Plugin Meta):**
   - **Primary Source (Billing & Shipping objects):**
     - Customer Name: `${payload.billing?.first_name || payload.shipping?.first_name || ""} ${payload.billing?.last_name || payload.shipping?.last_name || ""}`.trim() || "Client"
     - Phone: `payload.billing?.phone || payload.shipping?.phone`
     - Wilaya: `payload.shipping?.state || payload.billing?.state` (stripping leading `"DZ-"` or `"dz_"` prefix)
     - City/Commune: `payload.shipping?.city || payload.billing?.city`
     - Address Note: `[payload.shipping?.address_1, payload.shipping?.address_2].filter(Boolean).join(", ")` or billing address
     - Postcode: `payload.shipping?.postcode || payload.billing?.postcode` (if 5-digit Algerian postal code like `"13000"`, extracts first 2 digits `"13"`)
   - **Fallback Source (`meta_data` array):**
     When primary fields are missing, empty, or generic, inspect the top-level `meta_data` array:
     - Phone: keys matching `/(?:phone|téléphone|telephone|tel|هاتف|تلفون)/i` (e.g., `_billing_phone`)
     - Wilaya: keys matching `/(?:wilaya|province|state|ولاية)/i` (e.g., `_billing_wilaya`, `wilaya`)
     - Commune: keys matching `/(?:commune|city|بلدية|baladiya)/i` (e.g., `commune`, `baladiya`)
     - Address: keys matching `/(?:address|adresse|عنوان)/i` (e.g., `_billing_address_1`, `adresse`)
     - Name: keys matching `/(?:^nom$|^name$|^full[_\s]?name$|اسم)/i`

3. **Normalization via `@akadli/dz-geo` & `@akadli/core`:**
   - Phone is normalized to 10-digit local format (`05/06/07XXXXXXXX`) or E.164 (`+213...`).
   - Wilaya is resolved across all 69 Algerian Wilayas (2026 administrative division) via `normalizeWilaya(...)`.
   - Commune is resolved against valid communes for the resolved Wilaya via `normalizeCommune(..., wilayaCode)`.
   - Populates constraints (`allowedWilayas`, `allowedCommunes`, `allowedVariants`) and builds a canonical `StandardizedDzOrder`.

---

## 3. Order Decision Mutation (`applyOrderDecision`)

Once the customer concludes the voice confirmation call, the order decision is pushed to the WooCommerce REST API (v3).

### Required Credentials
```typescript
export interface WooCommerceCredentials {
  siteUrl: string;          // WordPress/WooCommerce site URL (e.g. "https://dz-store.com")
  consumerKey: string;      // WooCommerce REST API Consumer Key (ck_...)
  consumerSecret: string;   // WooCommerce REST API Consumer Secret (cs_...)
  cancelOnRefused?: string; // Default: "true" ("false" to skip status: "cancelled")
}
```

### Outbound REST Endpoints

All requests use HTTP Basic Authentication:
- `Authorization: Basic ${Buffer.from(`${consumerKey}:${consumerSecret}`).toString("base64")}`
- `Content-Type: application/json`

Base endpoint: `{siteUrl}/wp-json/wc/v3`

#### 1. `CONFIRMED`
- `PUT /wp-json/wc/v3/orders/{orderId}`:
  ```json
  {
    "meta_data": [
      { "key": "_akadli_status", "value": "akadli-confirmed" }
    ]
  }
  ```
- `POST /wp-json/wc/v3/orders/{orderId}/notes`:
  ```json
  {
    "note": "[Akadli-AI] Order CONFIRMED by customer (akadli-confirmed).",
    "customer_note": false
  }
  ```

#### 2. `MODIFIED`
- `PUT /wp-json/wc/v3/orders/{orderId}`:
  ```json
  {
    "shipping": {
      "state": "13",
      "city": "Maghnia",
      "address_1": "Nouvelle adresse près du stade"
    },
    "billing": {
      "state": "13",
      "city": "Maghnia",
      "address_1": "Nouvelle adresse près du stade"
    },
    "meta_data": [
      { "key": "_akadli_status", "value": "akadli-modified" },
      { "key": "_akadli_variant", "value": "XL" }
    ]
  }
  ```
- `POST /wp-json/wc/v3/orders/{orderId}/notes`:
  ```json
  {
    "note": "[Akadli-AI] Order MODIFIED: Variant -> XL; Wilaya -> 13; Commune -> Maghnia",
    "customer_note": false
  }
  ```

#### 3. `REFUSED`
- `PUT /wp-json/wc/v3/orders/{orderId}`:
  ```json
  {
    "status": "cancelled",
    "meta_data": [
      { "key": "_akadli_status", "value": "akadli-refused" }
    ]
  }
  ```
- `POST /wp-json/wc/v3/orders/{orderId}/notes`:
  ```json
  {
    "note": "[Akadli-AI] Order REFUSED: Customer ordered by mistake and asked to cancel.",
    "customer_note": false
  }
  ```

# FILE: @akadli/provider-gsheets - README.md

**[English](./README.md) | [🇩🇿 العربية](./README.ar.md)**

# @akadli/provider-gsheets

> Universal Google Sheets & Apps Script bridge for Algerian COD landing pages and entry-level store builders (SetShop, JustSell, Foorweb).

Implements `IEcommerceProvider` from `@akadli/adapter-contract` supporting flexible Arabic, French, and English column headers, HMAC/secret verification, and two-way cell mutations.

---

## Connection Modes for Algerian Merchants

### Mode A: Direct Google Sheets REST API v4
Connects directly using a Google Cloud Service Account OAuth token. Requires `spreadsheetId` and `accessToken`.

### Mode B: Zero-OAuth Google Apps Script Web App (Recommended for Fast Setup)
Merchants deploy a simple Web App inside their Google Sheet that handles outbound webhooks and accepts post-call updates.

#### Copy-Paste Google Apps Script (`doPost` Handler)
Inside your Google Sheet -> **Extensions** -> **Apps Script**, paste:

```javascript
function doPost(e) {
  var data = JSON.parse(e.postData.contents);
  var sheet = SpreadsheetApp.getActiveSpreadsheet().getSheetByName("Sheet1");
  var row = data.rowNumber;
  if (!row) return ContentService.createTextOutput("Missing rowNumber");

  sheet.getRange(row, 7).setValue(data.status); // Col G: Status
  if (data.finalWilaya) sheet.getRange(row, 9).setValue(data.finalWilaya); // Col I: Wilaya
  if (data.finalCommune) sheet.getRange(row, 10).setValue(data.finalCommune); // Col J: Commune
  if (data.reasonOrNotes) sheet.getRange(row, 12).setValue(data.reasonOrNotes); // Col L: Notes
  return ContentService.createTextOutput("OK");
}
```
*Deploy as Web App -> Execute as: Me -> Who has access: Anyone.*

---

## Credentials Schema

| Mode | Field | Type | Required | Default | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **A** | `spreadsheetId` | `string` | Yes (Mode A) | — | Google Sheet ID from URL |
| **A** | `accessToken` | `string` | Yes (Mode A) | — | Google Cloud OAuth2 token |
| **A** | `sheetName` | `string` | No | `"Sheet1"` | Target tab name |
| **A** | `statusColumn` / `notesColumn` | `string` | No | `"G"` / `"L"` | Columns for status and notes |
| **B** | `appsScriptWebhookUrl` | `string` | Yes (Mode B) | — | Deployed Apps Script Web App URL |
| **B** | `secret` | `string` | No | — | Shared secret token for verification |

---

## Usage Example

```typescript
import { GSheetsProvider } from "@akadli/provider-gsheets";

const provider = new GSheetsProvider();

// 1. Verify Webhook (supports x-akadli-signature hex HMAC or x-akadli-secret)
const isValid = await provider.verifyWebhook(headers, rawBody, process.env.GSHEETS_WEBHOOK_SECRET!);

// 2. Parse row payload (supports Arabic headers like 'الاسم', 'الهاتف', 'الولاية')
const order = await provider.parseWebhookOrder(JSON.parse(rawBody));

// 3. Mutate Google Sheet row (Mode B Apps Script or Mode A REST API)
const result = await provider.applyOrderDecision(order.orderId, {
  orderId: order.orderId,
  status: "CONFIRMED",
  reasonOrNotes: "Confirmed via voice agent"
}, {
  appsScriptWebhookUrl: process.env.GSHEETS_APPS_SCRIPT_URL!
});
```

# FILE: @akadli/provider-gsheets - docs/api-spec.md
================================================================================


# Google Sheets Algerian COD Adapter Specification (`@akadli/provider-gsheets`)

This document defines the technical specification, webhook signature verification, Algerian COD sheet row extraction, and outbound mutation endpoints for Google Sheets integrating with the **Akadli-AI** voice confirmation engine.

---

## Background: Why Google Sheets Integration is Critical

In the Algerian e-commerce ecosystem, entry-level store builders (such as **SetShop**, **JustSell**, **DZBuild**, and **Foorweb**) as well as custom single-product COD landing pages do not expose full-featured two-way REST APIs for order management. Instead, they sync every incoming checkout submission into a **Google Sheet row** and trigger an outbound webhook via Google Apps Script (`UrlFetchApp`).

`@akadli/provider-gsheets` acts as the universal bridge for these platforms, enabling:
1. Ingesting new order rows with flexible multi-lingual column headers (Arabic, French, English).
2. Normalizing Algerian customer phone numbers and 2026 Wilayas/Communes.
3. Mutating the Google Sheet row directly upon voice call completion via either:
   - **Mode A**: Direct Google Sheets REST API v4 (`values:batchUpdate`).
   - **Mode B**: Google Apps Script Web App Webhook callback (`doPost`).

---

## 1. Webhook Signature Verification (`verifyWebhook`)

Google Apps Script webhooks emit payloads using `UrlFetchApp.fetch()`. Merchants can configure either a cryptographic HMAC-SHA256 signature header or a shared secret token header.

### Supported Headers
- **HMAC Signature:** `x-akadli-signature` or `x-gsheets-signature` (case-insensitive) containing the `hex` digest of HMAC-SHA256 over the unparsed raw body.
- **Shared Secret / Token:** `x-akadli-secret` (or `authorization: Bearer <secret>`).

### Verification Protocol
1. If `x-akadli-signature` or `x-gsheets-signature` is present:
   - Compute `crypto.createHmac("sha256", secret).update(bodyBuffer).digest("hex")`.
   - Compare with the signature using `crypto.timingSafeEqual` after verifying byte lengths match.
2. If `x-akadli-secret` is present:
   - Compare header value with configured `secret` using `crypto.timingSafeEqual` over UTF-8 buffers of equal length.
3. If neither header matches or signatures differ, return `false` gracefully without throwing unhandled exceptions.

```typescript
import { createHmac, timingSafeEqual } from "node:crypto";

export function verifyGSheetsWebhook(
  headers: Record<string, string>,
  rawBody: string | Buffer,
  secret: string
): boolean {
  if (!secret) return false;

  // Case-insensitive header lookup
  const getHeader = (name: string): string | undefined => {
    const key = Object.keys(headers).find((k) => k.toLowerCase() === name.toLowerCase());
    return key ? headers[key] : undefined;
  };

  const sigHeader = getHeader("x-akadli-signature") || getHeader("x-gsheets-signature");
  if (sigHeader) {
    const bodyBuffer = typeof rawBody === "string" ? Buffer.from(rawBody, "utf8") : rawBody;
    const computedHex = createHmac("sha256", secret).update(bodyBuffer).digest("hex");
    const sigBuf = Buffer.from(sigHeader.trim(), "utf8");
    const compBuf = Buffer.from(computedHex, "utf8");
    if (sigBuf.length === compBuf.length && timingSafeEqual(sigBuf, compBuf)) {
      return true;
    }
  }

  const secretHeader = getHeader("x-akadli-secret");
  if (secretHeader) {
    const headerBuf = Buffer.from(secretHeader.trim(), "utf8");
    const secBuf = Buffer.from(secret.trim(), "utf8");
    if (headerBuf.length === secBuf.length && timingSafeEqual(headerBuf, secBuf)) {
      return true;
    }
  }

  return false;
}
```

---

## 2. Inbound COD Row Extraction (`parseWebhookOrder`)

Google Sheet rows arrive as JSON payloads containing row numbers and flexible column key mappings across English, French, and Arabic.

### Row Identification & Tracking
- Payload supplies either `rowNumber` (number or string like `42`) or `orderId` (e.g., `"ROW-42"` or `"SS-1042"`).
- `@akadli/provider-gsheets` preserves the `rowNumber` in the canonical `orderId` (e.g. `ROW-42` or `SS-1042#ROW-42`), ensuring that `applyOrderDecision` can target the exact row on Google Sheets.

### Column Key Mapping
Column keys are evaluated case-insensitively, supporting trimmed Arabic, French, and English variations:

| Field | Accepted Candidate Keys | Default Fallback |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Customer Name** | `full_name`, `nom`, `client`, `الاسم`, `اسم_العميل`, `name`, `customer` | `"Client"` |
| **Phone** | `phone`, `telephone`, `tel`, `الهاتف`, `رقم_الهاتف`, `mobile` | Must normalize via `@akadli/dz-geo` |
| **Wilaya** | `wilaya`, `province`, `state`, `الولاية`, `region` | Must normalize to 2-digit code (`"01"`-`"69"`) |
| **Commune** | `commune`, `baladiya`, `city`, `البلدية`, `ville` | Must match or fallback to Wilaya capital |
| **Address Note**| `address`, `adresse`, `note`, `العنوان`, `address_note` | `""` |
| **Product** | `product`, `item_name`, `produit`, `المنتج`, `اسم_المنتج`, `article` | `"Article"` |
| **Size / Variant** | `size`, `taille`, `variant`, `المقاس`, `الحجم` | `"Standard"` |
| **Price (DZD)** | `price`, `total`, `prix`, `السعر`, `montant` | `0` |

### Normalization Pipeline
1. Ingest flat or nested row payload (`payload.data` / `payload.row` / top-level keys).
2. Phone normalized to 10-digit Algerian format (`05/06/07XXXXXXXX`) via `normalizeDzPhone(..., "local")`.
3. Wilaya normalized to official 2-digit code (`"01"`-`"69"`) via `normalizeWilaya(...)`.
4. Commune normalized within the resolved Wilaya via `normalizeCommune(...)`.
5. Canonical order created via `createStandardizedDzOrder(...)` from `@akadli/core`.

---

## 3. Order Decision Mutation (`applyOrderDecision`)

Post-call decisions (`CONFIRMED`, `MODIFIED`, `REFUSED`) are mutated back into Google Sheets. Two execution modes are supported:

### Mode A: Direct Google Sheets REST API v4 (Google Cloud Service Account / OAuth)

Used when `credentials.spreadsheetId` and `credentials.accessToken` are provided.

#### Credentials Schema
```typescript
export interface GSheetsApiCredentials {
  spreadsheetId: string;
  accessToken: string;
  sheetName?: string;      // default: "Sheet1"
  statusColumn?: string;   // default: "G"
  sizeColumn?: string;     // default: "H"
  wilayaColumn?: string;   // default: "I"
  communeColumn?: string;  // default: "J"
  addressColumn?: string;  // default: "K"
  notesColumn?: string;    // default: "L"
  baseUrl?: string;        // default: "https://sheets.googleapis.com"
}
```

#### Mutation Endpoint
- **Method:** `POST {baseUrl}/v4/spreadsheets/{spreadsheetId}/values:batchUpdate`
- **Headers:**
  - `Authorization: Bearer {accessToken}`
  - `Content-Type: application/json`
- **Payload (`valueInputOption: "USER_ENTERED"`):**
```json
{
  "valueInputOption": "USER_ENTERED",
  "data": [
    {
      "range": "Sheet1!G42",
      "values": [["akadli-confirmed"]]
    },
    {
      "range": "Sheet1!L42",
      "values": [["Confirmed by customer via voice call"]]
    }
  ]
}
```

For `MODIFIED` decisions, `sizeColumn`, `wilayaColumn`, `communeColumn`, and `addressColumn` are included in the `data` array if specified in the decision.

### Mode B: Apps Script Webhook Callback URL

For merchants without Google Cloud API credentials, a Google Apps Script Web App URL can be configured.

#### Credentials Schema
```typescript
export interface GSheetsAppsScriptCredentials {
  appsScriptWebhookUrl: string;
  secret?: string;
}
```

#### Callback Request
- **Method:** `POST {appsScriptWebhookUrl}`
- **Headers:**
  - `Content-Type: application/json`
  - `x-akadli-secret: {secret}` (if secret provided)
  - `x-akadli-signature: {hexHmac}` (if secret provided)
- **Body:**
```json
{
  "orderId": "SS-1042#ROW-42",
  "rowNumber": 42,
  "status": "CONFIRMED",
  "externalStatus": "CONFIRMED",
  "finalVariant": "43",
  "finalWilaya": "16",
  "finalCommune": "Bab Ezzouar",
  "finalAddressNote": "Cité 8 Mai 1945",
  "reasonOrNotes": "Confirmed with size change",
  "updatedAt": "2026-10-19T14:00:00.000Z"
}
```

---

## 4. Error Handling & HTTP Status Codes

- **401 / 403 Unauthorized:** Return `{ success: false, externalStatus: "UNAUTHORIZED", rawResponse: ... }`.
- **404 Not Found:** Return `{ success: false, externalStatus: "NOT_FOUND", rawResponse: ... }`.
- **Missing Row Number:** Return `{ success: false, externalStatus: "INVALID_ROW_NUMBER", rawResponse: ... }`.
- **Network / Other Errors:** Fail gracefully with descriptive error payloads.

# FILE: @akadli/provider-tassyir - README.md
================================================================================


**[English](./README.md) | [العربية](./README.ar.md)**

# @akadli/provider-tassyir

> Official Tassyir Admin API (2026-10) adapter with Standard Webhooks (v1a Ed25519 zero-secret public key verification & HMAC fallback), install-code OAuth (tsy_ic_...) with HTTP Basic Auth, idempotent order confirmations (Idempotency-Key), and Algerian COD address normalization.

Implements `IEcommerceProvider` from `@akadli/adapter-contract` for Algerian merchants and fulfillment hubs managing Cash on Delivery (COD) orders via **Tassyir** (`api.tassyir.io`).

---

## Tassyir App Configuration (tassyir.app.toml)

When developing a headless external application on the Tassyir Developer platform (`developers.tassyir.io`), configure your `tassyir.app.toml` file as follows:

```toml
name        = "Akadli"
handle      = "akadli"
api_version = "2026-10"

[access]
scopes = ["read_orders", "write_orders", "read_customer_contact", "read_products"]

[access.scope_reasons]
read_orders = "Read incoming COD orders for voice confirmation"
write_orders = "Confirm, modify, or cancel COD orders after voice call"
read_customer_contact = "Read buyer phone and address for confirmation call"
read_products = "Allows the adapter to fetch alternative sizes/variants"

[auth]
callback_url = "https://your-domain.com/api/webhooks/tassyir/callback"

[[webhooks]]
topics = ["orders/created"]
uri    = "/api/webhooks/tassyir"

[hosting]
mode = "external"
url  = "https://your-domain.com"
```

### Required App Scopes
- `read_orders`: Read incoming orders, line items, and customer delivery destinations.
- `write_orders`: Update order notes, confirm (`/confirm`), and cancel (`/cancel`) orders.
- `read_customer_contact`: **Mandatory for voice confirmation.** Without this scope (or if past merchant plan quota), phone numbers are masked as `"**********"` and the order enters `waiting: true`. The adapter detects this and throws an actionable error.
- `read_products`: Recommended for multi-variant products. Allows the adapter to fetch full size/variant choices from `GET /products/{productId}` so voice callers can switch sizes.

---

## Authentication & OAuth Flow

Tassyir external apps do not use static merchant API keys. Authentication uses OAuth 2.0 with install authorization codes:

1. **App Installation:** When a merchant installs the external app on their store, Tassyir redirects their browser to your configured `[auth] callback_url` with an install code:
   ```text
   GET https://<tunnel>/api/webhooks/tassyir/callback?code=tsy_ic_...
   ```
2. **Redeeming Install Code:** The backend redeems `tsy_ic_...` via `POST https://api.tassyir.io/apps/oauth/token`:
   - **Authentication:** HTTP Basic Auth header `Authorization: Basic base64(client_id:client_secret)`
   - **Content-Type:** `application/x-www-form-urlencoded`
   - **Body:** `grant_type=authorization_code&code=tsy_ic_...`
   - Note: Never pass `client_secret` in the request body; Tassyir rejects that with `invalid_client`.
   - **Response:**
     ```json
     {
       "access_token": "tsy_at_...",
       "refresh_token": "tsy_rt_...",
       "expires_in": 3600,
       "token_type": "Bearer",
       "installation_id": "inst_..."
     }
     ```
3. **Refreshing Tokens:** When the access token expires, refresh it using `grant_type=refresh_token&refresh_token=tsy_rt_...` with HTTP Basic Auth. The `TassyirClient` automatically handles this refresh.

---

## Standard Webhooks & Public Keys (Zero-Secret Verification)

Tassyir signs all inbound webhooks using the **Standard Webhooks (`v1a` Ed25519)** specification. Tassyir does **not** provide a per-store "webhook secret". Instead:

- Signatures are signed using an Ed25519 private key by Tassyir.
- Corresponding public keys (`whpk_<base64_raw_32_byte_ed25519_key>`) are published at:
  ```text
  GET https://api.tassyir.io/apps/webhook-keys
  ```
- The adapter decodes the 32-byte raw Ed25519 public key natively using standard 12-byte ASN.1 SPKI DER prefix (`302a300506032b6570032100` in hex) with Node's native `crypto.createPublicKey`:
  ```typescript
  const spkiDerPrefix = Buffer.from("302a300506032b6570032100", "hex");
  const der = Buffer.concat([spkiDerPrefix, raw32ByteKeyBuffer]);
  const keyObject = crypto.createPublicKey({ key: der, format: "der", type: "spki" });
  ```
- Public keys fetched from `https://api.tassyir.io/apps/webhook-keys` are cached in memory for 1 hour.
- An embedded fallback key (`whpk_1BaNZhSk1qxT/1RugRT9eucQWvfo1ufg0o1u5qZejAA=`) ensures offline and test resilience.
- For local unit testing and simulators, HMAC-SHA256 verification is supported when a non-`whpk_` secret is passed explicitly.

---

## Credentials Configuration (TassyirCredentialsSchema)

The adapter accepts either direct access tokens or OAuth application credentials:

| Field | Type | Required | Default | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `accessToken` | `string` | Optional* | — | Direct Tassyir Bearer access token (`tsy_at_...` or `apiKey` for backwards compatibility) |
| `clientId` | `string` | Optional* | — | Tassyir App Client ID (`app_...`) from Developer Console |
| `clientSecret` | `string` | Optional* | — | Tassyir App Client Secret (`tsy_cs_...`) from Developer Console |
| `refreshToken` | `string` | Optional | — | Tassyir OAuth Refresh Token (`tsy_rt_...`) for auto-refresh |
| `baseUrl` | `string` | No | `"https://api.tassyir.io/apps/2026-10"` | Tassyir Admin API base endpoint |
| `confirmOnModified` | `string` | No | `"true"` | Calls `/confirm` when an order is updated with new size/address |
| `cancelOnRefused` | `string` | No | `"true"` | Calls `/cancel` when an order is refused during a voice call |

\* Either `accessToken` or (`clientId` and `clientSecret`) must be provided.

---

## Usage Example

```typescript
import { TassyirProvider, TassyirClient } from "@akadli/provider-tassyir";

// 1. Initialize provider
const provider = new TassyirProvider();

// 2. Verify inbound webhook (zero-secret Ed25519 verification against published whpk_ keys)
const isValid = await provider.verifyWebhook(
  headers,
  rawBody
);

if (!isValid) {
  throw new Error("Invalid Tassyir Ed25519 signature");
}

// 3. Parse standardized Algerian COD order (supports 2026-10 envelope)
const order = await provider.parseWebhookOrder(JSON.parse(rawBody));

// 4. Apply post-call decision to Tassyir Admin API
const result = await provider.applyOrderDecision(
  order.orderId,
  {
    orderId: order.orderId,
    status: "CONFIRMED",
    reasonOrNotes: "Customer confirmed via ElevenAgents voice call",
  },
  {
    clientId: process.env.TASSYIR_CLIENT_ID!,
    clientSecret: process.env.TASSYIR_CLIENT_SECRET!,
    refreshToken: process.env.TASSYIR_REFRESH_TOKEN!,
  }
);

console.log("Mutation result:", result.externalStatus); // "CONFIRMED"
```

---

## OAuth Helper Methods on TassyirClient

```typescript
const client = new TassyirClient({
  clientId: process.env.TASSYIR_CLIENT_ID!,
  clientSecret: process.env.TASSYIR_CLIENT_SECRET!,
});

// Redeem merchant install code on callback redirect
const tokens = await client.redeemInstallCode(
  process.env.TASSYIR_CLIENT_ID!,
  process.env.TASSYIR_CLIENT_SECRET!,
  installCode
);
console.log("Access Token:", tokens.access_token);
console.log("Refresh Token:", tokens.refresh_token);

// Refresh expired token
const refreshed = await client.refreshAccessToken(
  process.env.TASSYIR_CLIENT_ID!,
  process.env.TASSYIR_CLIENT_SECRET!,
  tokens.refresh_token!
);
```
